title: Repossession and Collateral Recovery: One Case per Contract and Default Episode
content:
**Clause.** Under Repossession and Collateral Recovery, recovery cases are held per contract and per default episode: a borrower with several contracts may have a case on each, without a per-borrower limit, but one contract never has more than one case (the class limit of recovery cases not closed at once for one contract) in pre-repossession review, assigned or recovered status. A new case on the same contract opens only after the earlier case has closed (reinstated, redeemed, sold or recalled).

## The clause broken down

| Question | Answer under the clause |
|---|---|
| What is one case? | One default episode of one contract. |
| Is there a limit per borrower? | No per-borrower limit applies; each contract is counted on its own. |
| Which statuses count as open? | Pre-repossession review, assigned and recovered. |
| Which statuses count as closed? | Reinstated, redeemed, sold and recalled. |
| When may a second case open on the same contract? | Only after the earlier case of that contract has closed. |

## Cases (hypothetical borrowers)

- A borrower holds two Retail Installment Contracts and both fall into default: each contract may carry its own case at the same time.
- A contract's case is in recovered status and the same contract is referred again: no new case opens on that contract while the recovered case is open.
- A contract's earlier case closed as recalled: a later default on that contract may open a new case.
